<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `49e6550ad08256b76573ea0bb6e97d912a297dbc` — the merge of head `c41eb194965fe4833bcf55aded03474e5ed79bf3` into base `6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 49e6550ad08256b76573ea0bb6e97d912a297dbc && git checkout 49e6550ad08256b76573ea0bb6e97d912a297dbc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91 c41eb194965fe4833bcf55aded03474e5ed79bf3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91 && git merge --no-ff c41eb194965fe4833bcf55aded03474e5ed79bf3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c41eb194965fe4833bcf55aded03474e5ed79bf3`
Local-runs: probe — read `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.3 (the version `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins) from its npm tarball into the seat's scratch space, to check the PR's one behavioural claim
Scope: the net diff (7 files, +101/−5): `.changeset/24774-rotate-secret-cut-off-copy.md`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-application.object.ts`, the four `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/*.objects.generated.ts`, and `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/rotate-client-secret-copy.test.ts`. Read with them: `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.3, `rotateClientSecretEndpoint` (`dist/authorize-*.mjs`) and `validateClientCredentials` (`dist/utils-*.mjs`). Also the card #24774 with the claim 6289452299 and the dispatch 6289515613, the dev's `os-dev-report` 6290624826 (read as claims), the PR body, and the 41 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What rotation does: there is no grace period. Right, read in code.**
  - `rotateClientSecretEndpoint` generates a new secret and writes it with one `adapter.update` on `oauthClient`, setting `clientSecret` to the stored new value. No previous secret is kept.
  - `validateClientCredentials` checks a presented secret against `client.clientSecret` alone (`verifyStoredClientSecret`).
  - So the old secret is refused from the moment the update commits. The confirmation ("will stop working immediately") was already true, and the result dialog's grace-period sentence was the false one.
- **The fix: right.**
  - `resultDialog.description` now says the previous secret has already stopped working. The confirmation, the dialog's title, its acknowledgement and its `client_secret` field are byte-identical.
  - The new code comment states the handler's behaviour, and the reading above makes it true.
- **The translations: right.**
  - `en` is regenerated (one line, byte-equal to the source, pinned).
  - `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` carried a translated grace-period sentence, and the extractor keeps translated values in merge mode, so they were re-translated by hand, value only. Each new value says the old secret has already stopped working.
  - No other key in any bundle moves.
- **The pins have teeth:**
  - both source texts say the secret stops at once, and neither carries a grace term;
  - the dialog's other parts are kept;
  - `en` mirrors the source;
  - no locale promises a grace period in either text.

  The dev's two ablation legs (source, and `zh-CN`) go red as read.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `@objectstack/platform-objects`: right for a text-only change.
- `Clause-②: no (text only: …)` is at a line start in the changeset and the PR body. Check Changeset is green.
- Nothing widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1** (three translated values edited by hand): accepted. The tool keeps translated values in merge mode, AGENTS.md permits a value edit, and leaving them would ship the false sentence in three locales.
- **Deviation 2** (dependent suites narrowed to the consumers that read this action: `runtime` and `cli`): accepted. Nothing structural moved, and CI's Test Core is green.
- **Deviation 3** (the pin asserts copy): accepted. The wording is the defect here.
- **Deviation 4** (no booted measurement): accepted. The code leaves no doubt.
- **Open question:** A, copy follows the handler. B, a grace window in `plugin-auth`, would be a new auth capability with no pull. A is right on the four axes.
- **The out-of-scope note** (`content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` shows an illustrative `target` that is not the shipped route): no producer reads it. No filing gate is met, and it is noted in the PR only.
- **Siblings:** this PR is the only one of #24758, #24765 and #24774 that touches the translation bundles, so nothing needs re-deriving. Its merge with PR #24867 is clean.
- **Check-runs on `c41eb194965fe4833bcf55aded03474e5ed79bf3`:** `ci-failure` GREEN, all 41 completed, none failed.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24774-rotate-secret-copy`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
